items.title: Saudi Arabia says it intercepted a ballistic missile headed for Riyadh on Monday
items.summary: Saudi Arabia said it intercepted and destroyed a ballistic missile launched toward Riyadh on Monday, as King Khalid airport stayed shut. The past week's Houthi attacks have killed at least 20 people and wounded hundreds, per CNN's tally. Hours earlier, civil aviation said the airport stays closed until further notice (NOTAM: at least Oct 17) pending safety verification.

items.title: Coalition claims 136 Houthi targets destroyed; Sanaa airport hit Sunday
items.summary: The Saudi-led coalition says large-scale airstrikes destroyed 136 Houthi military targets — missile storage, command centers and depots — to degrade their ballistic-missile capability; Houthi-run Al-Masirah confirmed strikes in Saada province. Saudi forces also struck Sanaa International Airport on Sunday (no casualty reports yet, per Saba). The Houthis counter-claim 124 Saudi airstrikes over the weekend and say 91 people, mostly women and children, have been killed since Sept 3 (unverified); the UN puts the latest fighting's toll near 1,000 killed and 200,000+ displaced.

items.title: MBS reportedly pushing Trump to take military action against Houthis
items.summary: Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman has reportedly been pressing President Trump to take military action against the Houthis, who agreed to a ceasefire with the US last year. Trump said Saturday the US may join Saudi strikes — a reversal after Washington repeatedly declined Riyadh's requests. The decision point lands as the Houthis vow to keep hitting Saudi airports and the coalition vows a strong response.
